result.title: Depth-guided Geometric Adaptation for Few-shot Image Classification
result.comment: This work is accepted by The IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV) 2027
result.summary: Few-shot image classification (FSIC) frequently suffers from visual ambiguity, where background clutter and RGB appearance similarities hinder discriminative feature matching in data-scarce settings. To mitigate this, we propose DAFIC, a geometry-guided framework that incorporates monocular depth into representation learning, episodic adaptation, and dense support-query matching. DAFIC first learns geometry-aware token representations through RGB-D self-supervised pre-training. Subsequently, the Depth-guided Geometric Adaptation (DGA) module uses depth-derived geometry to refine patch representations with geometry-enriched class context while suppressing background interference. Spatial Bidirectional Patch Matching (SBiM) then performs bidirectional dense matching on the refined features, reducing sensitivity to spurious correspondences and background clutter. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks show that DAFIC achieves strong performance against existing methods, with ablation and robustness analyses supporting the effectiveness of coupling geometry-conditioned episodic adaptation with bidirectional matching for few-shot visual recognition.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DAFIC 框架，将单目深度引入 RGB-D 自监督预训练、depth-guided 的 episodic 几何适配与双向稠密 patch 匹配，以缓解 few-shot 分类中背景杂乱和 RGB 外观相似造成的视觉歧义。
AI.relevance_reason: 其深度引导的 patch 级几何细化与背景抑制、双向匹配，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选与几何信息保留提供可核查的方法线索，但原文不涉及推理期 latent 状态生成或动态计算。
